delta: A control whose only visible label text lives inside a responsive-hidden utility (e.g. Tailwind `hidden ... sm:inline`) has zero accessible name below that breakpoint unless an explicit aria-label is also set on the control itself — `hidden` is display:none, which removes the element from the accessibility tree entirely, not just from view. This is distinct from the existing sr-only/overflow-clipping delta family (r5/r11): those are about sr-only content escaping a clipping container it IS inside; this is about a visible-at-desktop label that simply does not exist in the DOM/AX tree at narrower widths. A single desktop-preset Lighthouse run cannot catch it — only a mobile-preset run or manual review does.
evidence: auto-dash-r13 lens1: b's ⌘K search-trigger button has its only text inside hidden ... sm:inline (Topbar.tsx:29-47) with no aria-label on the enclosing button, leaving it with zero accessible name at 390px (confirmed in b-390.png) — a real WCAG button-name gap that still let b pass the hard gate at a11y=95. c independently solved the identical UI position correctly by adding aria-label matching its desktop visible text (Topbar.tsx:31). This pattern was ALSO independently caught pre-judging in this same round: c itself originally had this exact bug on its own search button, caught by the hard gate's mobile-preset Lighthouse run (button-name audit, a11y=94, hard-failed) and fixed via the 1-fix loop before judging began — same bug, same round, caught twice by two different mechanisms (machine gate once, qualitative judge review once).

delta: The focus hard gate only Tab-scans the DEFAULT-rendered page — any interactive control that mounts only after a user action (e.g. a ⌘K command-palette search input, opened by keypress/click) is invisible to it even if the exact same dead outline-none-with-no-replacement idiom is present. In this round, 2 of 3 independently-generated candidates correctly gave their command-palette input a focus-within ancestor wrapper for a real visible focus signal (per page-brief-core §2 ancestor-indication allowance); the third defined outline-none with no replacement at all and no FOCUS_WITHIN-equivalent token anywhere in its token file, and this real accessibility defect passed the automated hard gate cleanly (a11y 100, focus 0 violations) purely because the palette is not reachable via the default page Tab order. This generalizes the existing state-branch-contrast coverage-gap pattern (page-brief-core: gates only scan the default render) from color-contrast to focus-visibility: designers must independently audit every interactive control that appears only after opening a modal/palette/drawer, since gate passage does not certify them.
evidence: lens1 (brief compliance): b/command-palette.tsx:64,76 has outline-none on the input with no focus-visible/focus-within replacement and tokens.ts never defines a FOCUS_WITHIN-equivalent token, despite the file docstring claiming the dead idiom is avoided repo-wide. a/CommandPalette.tsx:42 and c/command-palette.tsx:49 both correctly wrap the identical input pattern in a FOCUS_WITHIN class. b still scored a11y 100 and focus 0-violations on the automated hard gate because gate.mjs --target web only Tab-scans the default-rendered /dash-evolve/r14/b page, and the command palette is a modal only reachable via an explicit open action.

delta: When a GENERATE-stage archetype assignment names a dominant-visualization CATEGORY (e.g. "a spatial/geographic map") without also naming the property that makes that category real (e.g. an actual geographic projection or area-based placement, not arbitrary Cartesian node coordinates), an independently-generated candidate can silently converge on an adjacent, already-assigned category (a node-link graph) instead — even while a sibling candidate was explicitly assigned that adjacent category on purpose. Two candidates this round (a: assigned node-link dependency graph; b: assigned spatial/geographic map) ended up with near-identical dominant-visualization mechanics (fixed-coordinate nodes connected by SVG lines/paths, health-color edge encoding, click-to-select-and-highlight, and a detail panel with the same stat-grid + trend-chart + adjacency-chip-list composition) because bs hub coordinates were hand-placed Cartesian values, not a real projection — bs own in-app copy even self-disclaimed it ("Schematic hub-and-lane view, not a geographic tile map"). The archetype-assignment instruction named the category but not its defining constraint, so nothing forced b toward genuine spatial encoding once a plausible-looking node-and-edge layout was easier to build.
evidence: lens3 (archetype differentiation): "b also delivers a node-link graph, not a spatial/geographic map... Hub coordinates in data.ts:34-45 are hand-placed Cartesian (x/y ~90-880), not a projection, grouped only nominally by corridor... beyond the dominant-viz overlap, its secondary interaction model duplicates as almost feature-for-feature" — cites matching edge-encoding logic (a/topology-graph.tsx:57-84 vs b/network-map.tsx:73-88), matching select-and-highlight (a/topology-graph.tsx:29-36,61-65,91 vs b/network-map.tsx:77,90-122), and matching detail-panel composition (a/detail-panel.tsx:69-93 vs b/hub-detail-panel.tsx:38-88).

delta: A table-fixed + percentage-column-width table that correctly avoids a desktop horizontal scrollbar (per the grid-craft no-scrollbar rule) can still fail badly at narrow viewports (390px): once a column's percentage allocation compresses below the intrinsic minimum width of its whitespace-nowrap header/cell text, the text does not wrap or truncate — it visually bleeds outward into the neighboring column's space, producing illegible overlapping text. Because the table container itself never exceeds its bounds (no actual overflow occurs — the columns genuinely shrink to their allocated percentage), a scrollWidth-based sweep/overflow gate does not fire on this defect at all. This is a distinct failure mechanism from the existing sr-only-escapes-clipping-container and modal/toggle-hidden-focus coverage gaps: those are DOM/accessibility-tree gaps, this is a pure visual-collision gap invisible to any geometry-overflow check. The established fix pattern used elsewhere in the catalog (e.g. a calendar table collapsing to a day-grouped agenda list below ) is to swap the dense table for a fundamentally different mobile layout (stacked cards/list) below a breakpoint, not to let the same table's percentage columns keep shrinking indefinitely toward zero.

delta: A page with TWO independent wide-scrolling containers (each its own overflow-x-auto div holding a table/grid wider than its box) can leak document.documentElement.scrollWidth beyond the viewport at narrow widths even though EACH scroller individually clips correctly (its own scrollWidth>clientWidth is expected and fine, and neither scroller alone reproduces the leak) — confirmed by controlled A/B toggling within one candidate: the dominant-visualization matrix (its own overflow-x-auto, ~740px content in a ~320px box) rendered with zero page-level overflow at 390px when isolated, and a SECOND wide overflow-x-auto table elsewhere on the same page (min-w-[640px] + table-fixed, the r1-delta idiom for forced-desktop-width tables) also rendered with zero overflow when isolated — but with BOTH present on the same page, document.documentElement.scrollWidth read 100px over clientWidth at 390px while document.body.scrollWidth read exactly clientWidth (the leak is only visible at the documentElement level, not body — a distinct symptom from the known sr-only/containing-block family). Root cause not fully isolated (not border-collapse, not position:sticky, not the flex-root's own overflow, not width:max-content vs a literal pixel width — all ruled out by direct toggling) but the fix that resolved it is: replace the SECOND (non-dominant, ordinary tabular data) scroller's min-w+overflow-x-auto pattern with the percentage-column table-fixed + responsive-hidden-column pattern already proven in this catalog (r19/b's OrderTable.tsx) — i.e. do not give an ordinary data table its own forced-min-width horizontal scroller when the page already has a genuinely-wide dominant-visualization scroller; reserve overflow-x-auto for the one visualization that structurally needs it and make every other table participate in a no-scroll percentage layout instead.

Rewriting SegmentTable to percentage-column table-fixed with two low-priority columns (Starting, Active now) dropped via a responsive-hidden utility below sm (no overflow-x-auto, no min-w) resolved the leak immediately — reconfirmed 0 overflow at all six sweep widths (1280/1366/1440/1600/1920/390) via direct Playwright scrollWidth/clientWidth measurement, then via the full gate.mjs sweep gate.

delta: A board/kanban-centric dominant layout (dash-brief-v3 '캘린더/보드 중심' archetype) with N independently-scrolling columns does not need any overflow-x-auto container at all — rendering the columns via CSS Grid (e.g. grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-N) with each column given a bounded max-height + its own overflow-y-auto avoids introducing a horizontal scroller entirely, sidestepping the auto-dash-r20/a defect class (two independent wide overflow-x-auto containers polluting document.documentElement.scrollWidth even though each clips correctly alone) by construction rather than remediation. This generalizes r20/a's fix (replace a forced-min-width scroller with a percentage-column table-fixed layout) one level further: for a genuinely multi-column board archetype, the analogous move is to drop the horizontal-scroll idiom altogether in favor of a responsive grid, since a kanban board has no structural need for the columns to sit in one unbroken horizontal scroll track the way a wide data table does.
